docs.explain:
IFS takes pairs of test and result and returns the result of the first test that comes out TRUE. Tests and results alternate, so three bands need three tests and three labels. The order of the pairs decides the answer, because the first match wins and nothing below it is read.

Ben's 78 fails 90 and fails 80, then lands on the 70 test, so B6 shows C. The second screen labels Cleo's 85 as Pass, since Merit needs 90. Raise the pass bar to 86 and her own score falls through to the fallback.

Close the list with TRUE and a fallback, or a score under every test returns #N/A. Older versions of Excel have no IFS, so the same logic turns up as nested IFs, and those are worth being able to read.

errors.text: No test was TRUE and there was no TRUE fallback pair, so a score under the last band has nothing to return.
The pairs are uneven and a test has no result of its own.
The version of Excel in use has no IFS, or the name is mistyped.

seo.title: IFS in Excel: more than two outcomes
seo.description: IFS is IF with more than two outcomes. It takes tests and results in pairs and returns the first true one, so order carries the logic.
